We cover what each app does, where it breaks, and how the pricing works in practice.[Tsenta](https://tsenta.com/) is one of the few agents in this comparison that submits complete applications on supported employer systems from iOS and Android, with an inspectable receipt for every successful send.


## Why Use a Mobile App to Apply for Jobs?


Job openings do not wait for you to get home and open a laptop. Many candidates prioritize applying early, and that window often falls while you are on a train, in a lecture, between meetings, or on a coffee break. A mobile-first workflow removes that delay. Research from the St. Louis Fed found that[41 percent of applications](https://www.stlouisfed.org/on-the-economy/2017/november/how-quickly-people-apply-jobs) arrive within the first 48 hours of a posting and 56 percent within the first 96 hours.


### Common Problems Mobile Job Seekers Run Into


- Career pages that render poorly in mobile browsers
- ATS login and multi-step forms that punish thumbs
- Résumé and cover letter files stored on a laptop, not your phone
- Screening questions repeated across many different portals
- Limited proof of what actually got submitted


Many mobile job apps primarily solve the discovery problem. You still swipe or tap through to the company site and finish the application by hand. Tsenta closes that loop by preparing job-specific materials from your saved candidate context and submitting complete applications on supported employer systems, including Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, and others.


## What to Look for in a Mobile App to Apply for Jobs


The category is noisy, and most tools benefit from vague marketing language. Cut through it by checking these features specifically.


### Features That Actually Matter


- **End-to-end submission on supported employer systems** , not just autofill on job boards
- **Coverage of employer systems** where jobs live, including Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby
- **Per-role tailoring** of résumé content using your saved background
- **Review controls** so you decide how much oversight to apply
- **A receipt** for every successful submission
- **Native iOS and Android apps** , not just a mobile browser view
- **Transparent, capped pricing**


Tsenta evaluates itself and its competitors against this list. The Tsenta agent surfaces relevant roles, prepares job-specific materials, submits complete applications on supported systems, keeps a receipt for successful submissions, runs on live iOS and Android apps, and publishes pricing with defined monthly caps. Review controls are available, and cover letters are prepared when supported or required by the employer system.


## How Job Seekers Use Mobile Apps to Apply


The primary audience for mobile auto-apply is people who are running high-volume searches and cannot afford to be tethered to a laptop.


**New grads and bootcamp grads:** Applying to many relevant roles from campus, commutes, and cafés.


**International students on F-1 or OPT:** Managing an authorization window and filtering for sponsorship signals. Post-completion OPT students are generally allowed up to[90 days of unemployment](https://internationaloffice.berkeley.edu/students/employment/opt) during the initial OPT period, which is why timing matters for this group. Employer sponsorship policies can change, so Tsenta surfaces known signals rather than making guarantees.


**Software engineers, data, and product managers:** Applying across many companies at once and using the phone to react when a match lands.


**Early-career finance and consulting candidates:** Managing time-pressured recruiting cycles where submission timing matters.


Across all four groups, the pattern is the same. Get a notification, review the match, approve it, and let the agent submit on supported systems. Tsenta is designed for that pattern.

### 2. Sorce


Sorce is a mobile-first job search app with a swipe-based interface and AI auto-apply on roles you approve.


**Key Features:**


- Swipe interface for role approval
- AI auto-apply on approved roles
- Cover letter generation on submitted applications
- Mobile-first UX


**Mobile-Specific Offerings:** iOS and Android apps with a swipe-and-apply flow.


**Pricing:** A free daily allowance and paid options are available. Verify current limits in the app.


**Pros:**


- Free-tier entry point on iOS and Android
- Purpose-built for mobile
- Simple approval flow


**Cons:**


- Swipe workflow may not suit candidates who want a slower review process
- Coverage varies by employer flow
- Volume is tied to daily usage limits


Sorce is a good fit if you want a swipe interface and are applying primarily through its supported flows. If your target roles live on Workday, Greenhouse, or Lever, evaluate coverage carefully.


### 3. LazyApply


LazyApply is a browser extension focused on high-volume applying, primarily on LinkedIn, Indeed, and ZipRecruiter.


**Key Features:**


- Browser extension for bulk applying
- Focus on major job boards
- Daily application caps that vary by plan


**Mobile-Specific Offerings:** Primarily a browser extension. Mobile use is limited compared with native apps.


**Pricing:** Annual plans are listed on the LazyApply site. Verify current pricing and application limits directly.


**Pros:**


- Built for job-board volume
- Simple setup for supported flows


**Cons:**


- Browser-extension form factor limits phone use
- Plans are oriented toward annual billing
- Coverage is weighted toward job-board apply flows rather than company employer systems


LazyApply can suit high-volume, job-board-led searches. It is a weaker fit when the goal is submitting to company employer systems from a phone.


### 4. JobCopilot


JobCopilot is a web-first auto-apply tool with review and autopilot options. It also includes résumé, interview-preparation, and tracking tools.


**Key Features:**


- Match-based auto-apply
- Review-before-submit and autopilot options
- AI mock interviews and career tools


**Mobile-Specific Offerings:** Mobile access is through its web experience rather than a native app.


**Pricing:** Paid plans are available. Verify current pricing and trial terms on the official site.


**Pros:**


- Broad career tooling
- Bundled résumé, cover letter, and mock interview tools
- Review mode provides oversight


**Cons:**


- Web-first experience is less phone-native
- Broad feature set may be more than users need for submission alone
- Exact coverage varies by plan and employer flow


JobCopilot can fit users who want broader career tools in one product. For phone-first workflows, compare its mobile web experience with native alternatives.


### 5. AIApply


AIApply combines résumé and career tools with an auto-apply product. It has a publicly listed iPhone app, and its broader toolset is also available through the web.


**Key Features:**


- Résumé builder, cover letter generator, and mock interview tools
- Auto-apply with adjustable review modes
- Job matching and application records


**Mobile-Specific Offerings:** A publicly listed iPhone app and mobile web access.


**Pricing:** Pricing varies by plan and add-ons. Verify current figures on the official site or in the app.


**Pros:**


- Broad résumé and interview toolkit
- Mobile option for iPhone users
- Multiple review and automation modes


**Cons:**


- Pricing and add-ons can be harder to compare
- Android availability is less clear than iPhone availability
- Employer-system coverage varies by workflow


AIApply is worth considering if you value the toolkit around applying. Compare its employer-system coverage and total plan cost with your target workflow.


### 6. LoopCV


LoopCV runs campaign-based automation across supported job boards. Users configure criteria and materials, then let the campaign scan and act on matches.


**Key Features:**


- Autopilot across supported job boards
- Match filters and volume controls
- Free tier to test match quality


**Mobile-Specific Offerings:** Web-based dashboard with mobile browser access.


**Pricing:** A free tier and paid plans are available. Verify current pricing directly.


**Pros:**


- Free tier to test
- Broad job-board scanning
- Campaign-style workflow


**Cons:**


- Web-first rather than native mobile
- Focuses more on job boards than deep employer-system coverage
- Application depth varies by source and setup


LoopCV is a solid pick for board-based campaigns. It is a different product from an agent that submits on company employer systems with a receipt.


### 7. Simplify


Simplify is a browser extension and mobile-web tool that autofills application fields and tracks applications. It remains an assistive tool rather than an end-to-end submission agent.


**Key Features:**


- Autofill on employer forms
- Application tracker
- Résumé builder


**Mobile-Specific Offerings:** Mobile web access. Autofill is browser-extension based.


**Pricing:** A free tier is available with paid upgrades.


**Pros:**


- Useful autofill on employer forms
- Application tracker
- Free entry point


**Cons:**


- Users still finish and submit applications themselves
- Mobile workflow is limited by the browser-extension model
- Focuses on assistance rather than full submission


Simplify is a good tracker and autofill helper. If you want an app that submits supported application workflows, compare full application agents instead.


## Evaluation Rubric: How We Ranked Mobile Job Application Apps


We scored each app across six categories. Weighting reflects what matters most for phone-first, high-volume job seekers.


- **End-to-end submission (25%):** Does the app actually submit, or does it only autofill?
- **Employer system coverage (20%):** Does it work on Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, and other employer systems?
- **Mobile experience (20%):** Is there a native iOS and Android app, or just a mobile browser view?
- **Pricing transparency (15%):** Are tiers and caps published clearly?
- **Materials quality (10%):** Are résumés prepared per role, with cover letters when supported or required?
- **Receipts and control (10%):** Can you inspect successful submissions and use review controls?


Tsenta ranks first in this comparison because it combines end-to-end submission and coverage of supported employer systems with live iOS and Android apps.
